question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [-1,0]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=5x{y}^{2}-2xy-{x}^{2}+3y. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,-1]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration. Round the answer for ${x}_{1}$ to **three decimal places**.
$[$ $-2$ {{field-1}} $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ $-5$ $]$
{{field-2}} $10$ {{field-3}}
${x}_{1}≈[$ {{field-4}} $]$
$-0.524$
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(5x{y}^{2}-2xy-{x}^{2}+3y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(5x{y}^{2}-2xy-{x}^{2}+3y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}-2y-2x \\ 10xy-2x+3\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(5{y}^{2}-2y-2x) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(10xy-2x+3) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(5{y}^{2}-2y-2x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(10xy-2x+3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 10y-2 \\ 10y-2 & 10x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 10y-2 \\ 10y-2 & 10x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}-2y-2x \\ 10xy-2x+3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 10y-2 \\ 10y-2 & 10x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}-2y-2x \\ 10xy-2x+3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & 10(-1)-2 \\ 10(-1)-2 & 10(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}5(-1)^{2}-2(-1)-2(1) \\ 10(1)(-1)-2(1)+3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & -12 \\ -12 & 10\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}-29/82 \\ 39/82\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{29}{82} \\ \frac{39}{82}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{29}{82} \\ \frac{39}{82}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.646 \\ -0.524\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
